questions.question:
Select the option that will improve the given sentence by using the most appropriate verb.

That Macbook belong to Xavier.

options.text: That Macbook is belonged to Xavier.
That Macbook is belong to Xavier.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb tense.
 
• The verb "**belong**" should be in the present tense "belongs" to agree with the singular subject "Macbook."
 
• The correct sentence structure should be "That Macbook belongs to Xavier," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

**Correct Sentence:** *"That Macbook belongs to Xavier."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "That Macbook is belonged to Xavier." - The verb phrase "is belonged" is incorrect as "belong" does not take a form like this.
 
• **Option 2:** "That Macbook belonging to Xavier." - This is a fragment and not a complete sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** "That Macbook is belong to Xavier." - This is grammatically incorrect as it combines "is" and "belong" incorrectly.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The teacher was / taken back by / the audacity of / the new student.

A B C D
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the phrase** "taken back."**
 
• The correct phrase should be "taken aback," which means surprised or shocked.
 
• **"Taken back"** incorrectly implies being returned to a previous position.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The teacher was taken aback by the audacity of the new student."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Segment D:** "the new student." - This part of the sentence is grammatically correct.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate article to fill in the blank.

_________ bed you sleep in is broken.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The definite article "**the**" is used when referring to something specific or something that has already been mentioned.
 
• In this context, "**the bed**" refers to a specific bed that is known to both the speaker and the listener.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The bed you sleep in is broken."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "On" - This is a preposition, not an article.
 
• **Option 2:** "An" - "An" is an indefinite article used before words that start with a vowel sound, not suitable here.
 
• **Option 3:** "A" - "A" is an indefinite article used before words starting with a consonant sound, not suitable here as the sentence refers to a specific bed.

questions.question:
Identify the grammatical error in the following sentence and select the correct tense from the options given below.

I have met my friend yesterday
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The present perfect tense **("have met")** should not be used with specific time expressions like "**yesterday**."
 
• The correct tense to use in this context is the simple past tense **("met")**.

**Correct Sentence:** *"I met my friend yesterday."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "have been meeting" - This is the present perfect continuous tense and is incorrect for a single event that happened yesterday.
 
• **Option 3:** "had been meeting" - This is the past perfect continuous tense and would imply an ongoing action leading up to another past action, which is not suitable here.
 
• **Option 4:** "was meeting" - This is the past continuous tense and implies an action was in progress at a specific time in the past, which is not suitable for a completed action like meeting a friend once.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• The word **"upshot"** means the final or eventual outcome or conclusion of a discussion, action, or series of events. (परिणाम)

 
 
• **Example:** The upshot of the meeting was a new policy that everyone agreed on.
 
 
 
• **"Cause"** refers to something that produces an effect, result, or condition; it is the reason why something happens. (कारण)
 
 
• **Example:** The cause of the fire was determined to be faulty wiring.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'upshot'** is **'cause'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 2**.

• **Result** (परिणाम): The outcome or consequence of an action or event.

 
 
• **Example:** The result of the test was better than expected.
 
 
 
• **Estimate** (अनुमान): An approximate calculation or judgment of the value, number, quantity, or extent of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The estimate for the project cost was around $5000.
 
 
 
• **Blame** (दोष): Assign responsibility for a fault or wrong.
 
 
• **Example:** He took the blame for the mistake to protect his team.
